backlog.title: Bench-complete fill-controller firmware (MVP)
backlog.description: Implement the entire PRD firmware contract (states, button semantics, backstop timer model, sensor trip logic, faults, LED contract, safety invariants) as two files (sketch + config.h) on the arduino-pico core, with every behavioral rule unit-tested natively on the host via a pure-logic/hardware seam, ending with USB-only bench validation of flows 1 and 2 (PRD sections 3-10).

milestones.title: Scaffold, config.h and safe skeleton
milestones.description: Create the repo layout that builds in both Arduino IDE and PlatformIO, author config.h as the single tunables surface, establish the native-test seam, and land the non-negotiable safety skeleton: valve LOW as line 1 of setup(), hardware watchdog fed every loop pass, rollover-safe time utilities, unplug-safe serial logging.

tasks.title: Project scaffold with config.h and native test seam
tasks.description: Two-file firmware foundation per PRD section 3, plus the auxiliary native test environment that later subtasks rely on for TDD.

subtasks.title: Author config.h with every section-8 tunable
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Repo is greenfield (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/system_context.md) — this is the first firmware file. Verified from arduino-pico docs (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md): analogRead defaults to 10-bit; PRD section 8 thresholds are 12-bit counts, so config.h must additionally carry ADC_BITS=12 (sketch calls analogReadResolution(12) — see P1.M3.T1.S2).
2. INPUT: None (root subtask). PRD section 8 defaults verbatim; pin map section 2.1 (PIN_SENSOR1=26/A0, PIN_SENSOR2=27/A1, PIN_VALVE=15, PIN_LED=14).
3. LOGIC: Create firmware/config.h with grouped, unit-commented constexpr constants: Pins; Button (BUTTON_LONG_PRESS_MS=1000, BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS=40); Fill backstop (FRESH_BOOT_BACKSTOP_MIN=30, BACKSTOP_TABLE_MIN as a constexpr array of {recoveryMin, backstopMin} pairs {{2,44},{10,41},{20,38},{35,34},{60,30}}, PLUS5_MIN=5); Windows (CONFIRM_WINDOW_S=12, EARLY_WET_WINDOW_S=5, TRIP_MIN_ELAPSED_S=60); ADC/sensors (ADC_BITS=12, ADC_SAMPLES_PER_READING=32, READING_INTERVAL_MS=100, BASELINE_SETTLE_MS=2000, BASELINE_MIN=2000, BASELINE_MAX=4050, TRIP_DROP_COUNTS=350, DEBOUNCE_COUNT=8); LED patterns (DONE_PULSE_ON_MS/OFF_MS=200, DONE_PULSE_COUNT=3, DONE_GAP_MS=1000, FAULT_BLINK_MS=250, FAULT_PAUSE_MS=2000, ACK_BLINK_MS=100, USE_ONBOARD_RGB=true, RGB_BRIGHTNESS=60); Platform (SERIAL_BAUD=115200, WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_S=8). constexpr (not #define) so native tests can static_assert. Constants only — no functions.
4. OUTPUT: firmware/config.h includable by the sketch (P1.M1.T1.S2) and by every native test; single source of every tunable for all downstream subtasks.
5. DOCS: Mode A — the grouped unit-commented constants ARE the documentation surface (PRD section 8 'one place'); no separate doc file.

subtasks.title: Dual-build skeleton (Arduino IDE + PlatformIO) with proven native test seam
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PRD section 3 requires the firmware to be TWO files (sketch + config.h) that build in BOTH Arduino IDE (arduino-pico core, board 'Waveshare RP2040-Zero') and optionally PlatformIO (platform raspberrypi, board waveshare_rp2040_zero; verify the board id resolves at build time — fallback: generic pico board def). Recommended layout (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md and firmware_architecture.md): firmware/ sketch folder containing jug_filler.ino + config.h; platformio.ini at repo root with [platformio] src_dir/firmware plus [env:pico] and [env:native] (platform=native, Unity). Native seam: ALL hardware-touching code (setup/loop, pinMode/digitalWrite/analogRead, Serial, WS2812, watchdog) inside #ifdef ARDUINO; ALL pure logic unguarded; test/*.cpp files #include the .ino (it is plain C++ with explicit prototypes, so g++ compiles it).
2. INPUT: firmware/config.h from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create the layout. Minimal sketch: setup() line 1 drives PIN_VALVE LOW (section 10 invariant), then pinMode outputs (valve, LED off), Serial.begin(SERIAL_BAUD), analogReadResolution(ADC_BITS); loop() safe placeholder. One trivial native Unity test (test/test_seam.cpp) asserting config constants — proving 'pio test -e native' is green BEFORE any logic lands. Mock: native env needs no hardware; pico env is compile-only here (no upload).
4. OUTPUT: buildable skeleton + green native test run + the seam contract documented in the .ino header comment; every later pure-logic subtask lands in the unguarded region.
5. DOCS: Mode A — seed README.md with build instructions (Arduino IDE + PlatformIO + native tests); expanded later by P2.M1.T3.S1.

tasks.title: Safe-loop foundation: watchdog, time utilities, logging policy
tasks.description: The timing and supervision bedrock every other component consumes: wrap-safe millis arithmetic, hardware watchdog, and a serial logging policy that cannot stall the device when USB is absent.

subtasks.title: Rollover-safe time utilities (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: millis() is uint32_t wrapping ~49.7 days; the rollover-safe pattern (uint32_t)(now - since) >= interval is standard on arduino-pico (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md). Section 10 forbids delay(); all timing must flow through these helpers.
2. INPUT: Seam from P1.M1.T1.S2; config.h constants.
3. LOGIC: Pure, unguarded helpers in the sketch: uint32_t elapsedMs(uint32_t now, uint32_t since) and bool deadlinePassed(uint32_t now, uint32_t deadline). Clock is ALWAYS an injected parameter — no millis() calls inside logic. Native tests: wrap boundary 0xFFFFFFFF to 0x00000000, equality (0 elapsed), 1ms-after-deadline, large spans.
4. OUTPUT: helpers consumed by button service (P1.M2), sensor chain (P1.M3), timer model (P1.M4), LED engine (P1.M5), state machine (P1.M6).
5. DOCS: none — internal helpers, no user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: Hardware watchdog service and unplug-safe serial logging
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Verified from pico-sdk hardware/watchdog.h (shipped inside arduino-pico — plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md): watchdog_enable(delay_ms, pause_on_debug) with RP2040 MAXIMUM 8388 ms, so WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_S=8 (8000 ms) is legal; watchdog_update() feeds; watchdog_caused_reboot() reports reset cause. In service the board runs from the buck with USB unplugged (section 2.2) — logging must never stall the loop when no USB host is attached (never while(!Serial), keep writes small).
2. INPUT: Skeleton setup()/loop() from P1.M1.T1.S2; config WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_S, SERIAL_BAUD.
3. LOGIC: In the ARDUINO region: setup() enables the watchdog AFTER the first-line valve LOW; loop() calls watchdog_update() as its first statement each pass (section 10). Add logLine(const char* fmt, ...) wrapper over Serial — small, newline-terminated — plus boot banner logging reboot cause via watchdog_caused_reboot(). Mock: hardware watchdog cannot be native-tested; any pure formatting helper is split out and tested.
4. OUTPUT: supervised loop + logLine() used by all later logging subtasks (P1.M2.T2.S1, P1.M3.T1.S2, P1.M6.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — no config surface change; logging formats documented at P2.M1.T1.S1.

milestones.title: BOOTSEL button service
milestones.description: Turn the onboard BOOT button into a classified event stream (short/long, acting on release, debounced) exactly per PRD section 5.1, correcting the PRD's pseudo-pin prescription to the real arduino-pico BOOTSEL API.

tasks.title: Pure button classifier
tasks.description: Debounce + press-length classification that emits ShortPress/LongPress on release only.

subtasks.title: ButtonClassifier: 40ms debounce, 1000ms long threshold, events on release (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 5.1: contact debounce 40 ms (BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS); a press is long if held >= 1000 ms (BUTTON_LONG_PRESS_MS); BOTH short and long actions fire on RELEASE. Section 4 transient ack also keys off the long press.
2. INPUT: Time utilities from P1.M1.T2.S1; config constants from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Pure class ButtonClassifier with enum Event {None, ShortPress, LongPress}; method Event update(uint32_t nowMs, bool pressedRaw). Internally: debounce via stable-sample tracking over 40 ms; hold time measured from debounced press start; on debounced release emit Short (hold < 1000) or Long (hold >= 1000); reset for next press. Injected clock; zero hardware calls. Native tests: sub-40ms bounce spikes ignored; short release; long release; hold exactly 1000 ms -> Long; release at 999 ms -> Short; no event while still held; back-to-back presses.
4. OUTPUT: Event stream consumed by the fill state machine core (P1.M6.T1.S1) and hardware wiring (P1.M2.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

tasks.title: Wire the onboard BOOTSEL hardware
tasks.description: Sample the real button and feed the classifier, using the verified arduino-pico BOOTSEL API (not the PRD's pseudo-pin phrasing).

subtasks.title: Poll BOOTSEL bool object into classifier with event logging
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (BINDING PRD CORRECTION): Verified from arduino-pico source cores/rp2040/Bootsel.cpp (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md): BOOTSEL is a global __Bootsel OBJECT with operator bool() returning TRUE when pressed. PRD section 2.1's pinMode(BOOTSEL, INPUT_PULLUP) / digitalRead(BOOTSEL) pseudo-pin pattern DOES NOT EXIST in this core and would silently configure/read GPIO 0-1. Correct pattern: bool pressed = BOOTSEL; sampled each loop pass — no pinMode needed. Reading it can never enter the bootloader (bootloader entry requires BOOTSEL held during RESET), matching the PRD's intent.
2. INPUT: ButtonClassifier from P1.M2.T1.S1; logLine() from P1.M1.T2.S2; skeleton loop from P1.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: In the ARDUINO region: each loop pass sample BOOTSEL (true = pressed), feed classifier, log each event with hold duration via logLine (e.g. 'BTN short 213ms' / 'BTN long 1024ms'). Mock: none on device; classifier behavior is native-tested in P1.M2.T1.S1. Bench check (USB power only, buck disconnected per section 2.2): press/release/hold-1s produces correct log lines.
4. OUTPUT: hardware-sourced ButtonEvent stream consumed by the integration loop (P1.M6.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — log lines only; README operation section handled by P2.M1.T3.S1.

milestones.title: Sensor chain: ADC sampling, baseline, trip detection
milestones.description: Everything between the raw analog lines and boolean trip/fault verdicts: 12-bit averaged readings, dry-baseline capture with plausibility gate, the drop-threshold trip rule with debounce streak, and the early/false-trip guards.

tasks.title: Averaged ADC reading service
tasks.description: 32-sample averaged readings every 100 ms per sensor, plus the median helper baselines use, with the 12-bit resolution requirement enforced.

subtasks.title: ReadingAggregator + median helper (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 8: ADC_SAMPLES_PER_READING=32 samples averaged per reading; one reading pair per READING_INTERVAL_MS=100 ms; section 7.1 baselines are the MEDIAN of averaged readings.
2. INPUT: Time utilities from P1.M1.T2.S1; config constants from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Pure class ReadingAggregator: addSample(uint8_t sensor, uint16_t counts, uint32_t nowMs); bool readingDue(uint32_t nowMs); on due, emit averaged pair (avg1, avg2) computed over the last 32 samples (pre-fill with first sample so readings are valid before 32 collect). Plus free function uint16_t medianOf(uint16_t* values, size_t n) for baselines. Injected clock; no hardware. Native tests: exact averaging; cadence with injected clock incl. wrap; under-fill warmup; median odd/even; single-outlier robustness.
4. OUTPUT: averaged-reading stream consumed by baseline (P1.M3.T2.S1), trip detectors (P1.M3.T3.S1, P1.M3.T3.S2) and the fill engine (P1.M6.T1.S2).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: ADC hardware wiring: 12-bit resolution + raw-count commissioning log
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (BINDING): Verified from arduino-pico analog docs (plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md): analogRead DEFAULTS TO 10-BIT; analogReadResolution(int bits) exists. PRD section 8 thresholds (BASELINE_MIN=2000, BASELINE_MAX=4050, TRIP_DROP_COUNTS=350) are 12-bit counts — WITHOUT analogReadResolution(12) every dry baseline would read ~0-1023 and every fill would baseline-fault. Sensors: GP26=A0/ADC0, GP27=A1/ADC1 (GP26-GP29 are the only ADC-capable pins), 3.3 V full-scale reads ~4095.
2. INPUT: ReadingAggregator from P1.M3.T1.S1; skeleton + logLine from P1.M1.T1.S2 / P1.M1.T2.S2.
3. LOGIC: In the ARDUINO region: setup() calls analogReadResolution(ADC_BITS); loop() samples analogRead(PIN_SENSOR1)/(PIN_SENSOR2) and feeds the aggregator; periodic (1 Hz) raw-count log line 'S1=<counts> S2=<counts>' for commissioning (section 9.3 dry/wet observation). Mock: device-only; aggregator math native-tested in P1.M3.T1.S1.
4. OUTPUT: live averaged readings + raw-count logging consumed by the integration loop (P1.M6.T2.S1) and commissioning audit (P2.M1.T1.S1).
5. DOCS: Mode A — ensure the config.h ADC group comment states the 12-bit requirement and that counts assume 3.3 V full-scale.

tasks.title: Baseline capture and plausibility gate
tasks.description: The section 7.1 pre-valve gate: settle 2 s, median-of-averaged dry baselines, range check, refuse-to-open on failure.

subtasks.title: BaselineCapture: 2s settle, median-of-averages, BASELINE_MIN..MAX check (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 7.1: settle BASELINE_SETTLE_MS=2000 ms with the valve still closed, then read both sensors' dry baselines as the median of averaged readings; if either is outside BASELINE_MIN=2000..BASELINE_MAX=4050 counts, fault that sensor and REFUSE to open the valve (this also catches accidental starts with the jug already full / tips wet — expected dry range ~3000-3900 counts per section 9.3).
2. INPUT: Averaged readings from P1.M3.T1.S1 (ReadingAggregator + medianOf); time utilities P1.M1.T2.S1; config constants.
3. LOGIC: Pure class BaselineCapture: begin(uint32_t nowMs); phase Settle for 2000 ms (no baseline collection before it elapses — abort during settle is the FSM's business, P1.M6.T1.S2); then collect N=5 averaged readings per sensor; finish with per-sensor verdict enum {Ok, TooLow, TooHigh} and baseline values. Native tests: settle not shortcut at 1999 ms; boundary counts 2000 and 4050 inclusive pass; 1999/4051 fail; both-sensors-bad; median robust to one outlier reading.
4. OUTPUT: per-sensor plausibility verdicts + baseline values consumed by TripDetector (P1.M3.T3.S1) and the fill engine baseline phase (P1.M6.T1.S2, P1.M6.T1.S3 fault code path).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

tasks.title: Trip detection and false-trip guards
tasks.description: The section 7.3 trip rule and the section 7.6 guards that classify impossible trips as sensor faults.

subtasks.title: TripDetector: baseline-350 for 8 consecutive readings (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 7.3: an AVERAGED reading at or below (baseline - TRIP_DROP_COUNTS=350) for DEBOUNCE_COUNT=8 consecutive readings = that sensor tripped.
2. INPUT: Baselines from P1.M3.T2.S1; averaged readings from P1.M3.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Pure class TripDetector (one instance per sensor): void feed(uint16_t avg); bool tripped() — latched once tripped for the remainder of the fill; streak resets to zero on any reading strictly above the threshold. Native tests: exactly-8 streak trips; 7 qualifying readings then one above threshold resets the streak; boundary value exactly baseline-350 qualifies (inclusive); no re-trip noise after latch; sensor1/sensor2 independence.
4. OUTPUT: per-sensor latched tripped flags consumed by the fill engine (P1.M6.T1.S2) and guards (P1.M3.T3.S2).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: False-trip guards: TRIP_MIN_ELAPSED_S and EARLY_WET_WINDOW_S (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 7.6: any trip accepted before TRIP_MIN_ELAPSED_S=60 s of fill time, or any sensor reading wet during the first EARLY_WET_WINDOW_S=5 s, is a false trip / short -> fault that sensor. 'Wet' means at/below baseline - TRIP_DROP_COUNTS (same predicate as the trip rule).
2. INPUT: TripDetector from P1.M3.T3.S1; averaged readings; time utilities P1.M1.T2.S1; the valve-open timestamp will be supplied by the fill engine (P1.M6.T1.S2) — accept it as a parameter, do not track it here.
3. LOGIC: Pure guard functions: GuardVerdict evaluate(uint32_t nowMs, uint32_t valveOpenedAtMs, TripState s1, TripState s2, Reading avg1, Reading avg2) -> {Ok, EarlyTripFault(sensor), EarlyWetFault(sensor)}. 'Fill time' = time since valveOpenedAt. Native tests: trip at 59.9 s -> EarlyTripFault, at exactly 60.0 s -> Ok; wet reading at 4.9 s -> EarlyWetFault, at 5.1 s -> Ok; both sensors clean -> Ok; wrap-safe timestamps.
4. OUTPUT: guard verdicts consumed by the fill engine fault paths (P1.M6.T1.S2, P1.M6.T1.S3).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

milestones.title: Timer model: recovery clock and concave backstop
milestones.description: The section 6 backstop brain: RAM-only recovery clock, piecewise-linear concave table lookup, fresh-boot default, and +5-min stacking extensions on the active fill only.

tasks.title: Concave backstop table interpolation
tasks.description: Exact piecewise-linear interpolation over BACKSTOP_TABLE_MIN with end clamping — never padded.

subtasks.title: backstopMinutes(): piecewise-linear interp with clamps (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 6.2 table {{2,44},{10,41},{20,38},{35,34},{60,30}} minutes, piecewise-linear BETWEEN points, clamped at both ends (recovery <= 2 min -> 44; >= 60 min -> 30). The concave shape is deliberate (tank refills fast then slows); a straight line pads the mid-range in exactly the wrong direction — interpolate between the given knots only, add no smoothing or safety padding.
2. INPUT: BACKSTOP_TABLE_MIN from config.h (P1.M1.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: Pure function uint32_t backstopMinutes(uint32_t recoveryMin): linear interpolation between adjacent knots, clamped outside. Define rounding explicitly (floor to whole minutes) and document it in a comment. Native tests: exact values at all 5 knots; recovery 0/1/2 -> 44; 60/120/1440 -> 30; midpoints (e.g. recovery 6 -> between 44 and 41; 15 -> between 41 and 38); property: result is monotone non-increasing over recovery.
4. OUTPUT: minutes value consumed by the recovery-clock/deadline task (P1.M4.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

tasks.title: Recovery clock and fill deadline management
tasks.description: RAM-only tank history: reference at last valve-close, fresh-boot default, once-per-fill computation, stackable +5 extensions.

subtasks.title: RecoveryClock + FillDeadline: fresh-boot default, valve-open anchor, stacking +5 (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 6.1 (RAM only — no persistence, section 3): reference point = the moment the PREVIOUS fill's valve closed (fill end, whatever ended it — done, abort, or fault); recovery for a new fill = wall-clock time since that reference; fresh boot / any reset -> no history -> FRESH_BOOT_BACKSTOP_MIN=30. Section 6.2: every fill's backstop is computed ONCE at fill start; a long-press +5 (PLUS5_MIN, section 5.1) modifies only the ACTIVE fill's deadline, stacks, repeatable. Section 6 preamble: the backstop bounds how long the VALVE may stay open — anchor the deadline at the valve-open instant, not at the button press (the 2 s baseline settle precedes valve open). Section 5.3: any reset clears history (trivially true for RAM state — document it).
2. INPUT: backstopMinutes() from P1.M4.T1.S1; time utilities P1.M1.T2.S1; config constants.
3. LOGIC: Pure classes: RecoveryClock { recordFillEnd(uint32_t nowMs); bool hasHistory(); uint32_t recoveryMs(uint32_t nowMs); } and FillDeadline { computed at fill start via recoveryMs->backstopMinutes; anchor(uint32_t valveOpenedAtMs); bool expired(uint32_t nowMs); void extend5(); } with extend5 stacking (each call adds PLUS5_MIN). Native tests: fresh boot -> 30 min; history at 15 min recovery -> interpolated value (~36-37, assert computed); abort resets reference at abort instant; +5 twice moves deadline exactly 10 min; deadline expiry boundary; wrap-safe arithmetic.
4. OUTPUT: backstop/deadline objects consumed by the fill engine (P1.M6.T1.S2) and its +5 long-press handling; log inputs (recovery, table result, deadline) exposed for the backstop computation log line (section 3).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

milestones.title: LED signaling: pattern engine and drivers
milestones.description: The section 4 LED contract as a pure time-driven pattern engine plus two drivers: the authoritative external green LED on GP14 and the config-gated WS2812 mirror on GP16.

tasks.title: Non-blocking LED pattern engine (pure)
tasks.description: One engine producing every pattern in sections 4 and 7 from an injected clock — solid, off, done triple-pulse, fault blink groups, transient ack overlay.

subtasks.title: LedPatternEngine: Solid/Off/DonePulse/FaultBlink(n)/AckBlink overlay (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 4 table: FILLING/CONFIRM external LED solid (WS2812 blue solid); IDLE off; DONE = triple-pulse attention blink 3x(on 200 ms/off 200 ms) then off 1000 ms, repeat, until acknowledged (no timeout, section 11); FAULT = blink-code groups N x(on 250 ms/off 250 ms), off 2000 ms, repeat (N = fault code 1-3, section 7). Transient ack (section 4): on a +5 long-press during FILLING the LED blinks 3x quickly (on 100 ms/off 100 ms) then RESUMES solid — a one-shot overlay, valve stays open, fill timing unaffected.
2. INPUT: Time utilities P1.M1.T2.S1; config LED constants (DONE_PULSE_*, FAULT_*, ACK_BLINK_MS).
3. LOGIC: Pure class LedPatternEngine: setMode(Mode) with Mode in {Off, Solid, DonePulse, FaultBlink(uint8_t groups)}; triggerAck() starts the one-shot ack overlay; bool tick(uint32_t nowMs) -> ledOn. All cadences derived from config constants; zero delay(); injected clock. Native tests: done-pulse on/off instants at pattern boundaries and 1000 ms gap repetition; fault groups for n=1,2,3 then 2000 ms pause; ack overlay: 3 blinks in 600 ms then previous mode (Solid) resumes exactly; mode change mid-pattern resets phase cleanly; wrap-safe.
4. OUTPUT: boolean ledOn stream + mode/ack API consumed by drivers (P1.M5.T2.S1, P1.M5.T3.S1); modes set only by the fill engine (P1.M6.T1.S2).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

tasks.title: External green LED driver (GP14)
tasks.description: The authoritative indicator: GP14 through 330 ohm to the super-bright green LED.

subtasks.title: Drive GP14 from the pattern engine each loop pass
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 2.1: GP14 -> 330R -> LED anode, cathode -> GND; the external green LED is AUTHORITATIVE (WS2812 only mirrors). CONFIRM continues solid (section 4); DONE persists until acknowledged — no timeout (section 11). GPIO drive strength is ample for ~10 mA through 330R at 3.3 V.
2. INPUT: LedPatternEngine from P1.M5.T1.S1; skeleton from P1.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: In the ARDUINO region: pinMode(PIN_LED, OUTPUT) in setup (LED off initially); each loop pass digitalWrite(PIN_LED, engine.ledOn). Mode selection itself is the fill engine's job (P1.M6.T2.S1) — this subtask only drives the pin from the engine state. Mock: none on device; engine patterns native-tested in P1.M5.T1.S1.
4. OUTPUT: driven external LED consumed by the integration loop (P1.M6.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

tasks.title: WS2812 onboard mirror (GP16, config-gated)
tasks.description: Optional color-matched mirror on the onboard RGB LED, capped at brightness 60/255 per the power budget.

subtasks.title: Config-gated WS2812 mirror with color map and brightness cap
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: arduino-pico bundles a WS2812 PIO library (libraries/WS2812; class WS2812(pin, count, pio) with begin()/pixel-setting/show methods — verify exact method names against the installed core version at implementation; treat availability as verified per plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/external_deps.md). RP2040-Zero onboard WS2812 is on GP16 (firmware-only pin, section 2.1), powered from 3V3. Section 2.2: keep brightness <= RGB_BRIGHTNESS=60/255 — implement by SCALING the RGB values written (do not depend on a library brightness API).
2. INPUT: LedPatternEngine modes/ledOn from P1.M5.T1.S1; config USE_ONBOARD_RGB, RGB_BRIGHTNESS.
3. LOGIC: In the ARDUINO region, fully gated by USE_ONBOARD_RGB: construct the strip on GP16 with 1 pixel; color map per section 4 mirror column — IDLE off (black); FILLING and CONFIRM blue solid; DONE green following the done-pulse ledOn pattern; FAULT red following the fault ledOn pattern. Update the pixel only when engine output changes. Mock: none on device. Bench: verify mirror colors/patterns match the external LED.
4. OUTPUT: mirror output consumed by the integration loop (P1.M6.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

milestones.title: Fill lifecycle state machine and fault latching
milestones.description: The heart of sections 4, 5 and 7: a pure five-state engine orchestrating baseline, valve, trips, confirm window, done and latched faults — then the thin hardware integration loop wiring every service together.

tasks.title: Pure fill engine
tasks.description: State transition table, lifecycle orchestration and fault latching as one natively-testable engine.

subtasks.title: Five-state core: section 5.1 transition table + valve invariant (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 5.1 is the normative table (both actions fire on release): IDLE short -> START FILL (FILLING), IDLE long -> nothing; FILLING short -> abort (valve closed -> IDLE), FILLING long -> +5 min to this fill's backstop (stacks) + LED ack (stay FILLING); CONFIRM short/long -> ignored; DONE short -> acknowledge (light off -> IDLE), DONE long -> also acknowledges; FAULT short/long -> ignored. Section 10 invariants: the valve is only ever HIGH while in FILLING, and FILLING is entered ONLY by a human BOOT short-press from IDLE — no path (boot, watchdog reset, fault recovery, button) ever opens the valve automatically (sections 5.3, 7.9).
2. INPUT: ButtonClassifier events from P1.M2.T1.S1; time utilities P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Pure transition core: enum State {Idle, Filling, Confirm, Done, Fault}; struct Outputs {bool valveOpen; LedMode led; bool plus5Applied; bool acknowledged;}. Implement the table EXACTLY — every cell, including the ignored ones. Native tests: one test per table cell; boot initial state = Idle with valveOpen=false; property test — no event sequence (fuzz, seeded) ever yields valveOpen=true except via the Idle+ShortPress transition; abort long-press does nothing in Idle.
4. OUTPUT: transition function consumed by the lifecycle orchestrator (P1.M6.T1.S2).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: Lifecycle orchestration: baseline -> valve -> trip -> CONFIRM -> DONE (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 7 steps 1-9 with these clarifications (documented in plan/001_53984f832581/architecture/firmware_architecture.md): the 2 s settle/baseline phase runs INSIDE Filling with the valve still closed — a short-press abort during settle is honored and, like any fill end, restarts the recovery clock at the abort instant (section 6.1 'whatever ended it'); the backstop is COMPUTED once at fill start (button press) but its deadline is ANCHORED at the valve-open instant because it bounds valve-open time (section 6 preamble); first sensor trip closes the valve IMMEDIATELY then enters Confirm for CONFIRM_WINDOW_S=12 s waiting for the other sensor; Confirm success -> Done with the recovery-clock reference set to the valve-CLOSE instant (section 7.8); EVERY code path that ends a fill sets the valve pin LOW FIRST (section 7.9) — engine output ordering must reflect close-before-state-flip.
2. INPUT: FSM core (P1.M6.T1.S1); BaselineCapture (P1.M3.T2.S1); TripDetectors (P1.M3.T3.S1); guards (P1.M3.T3.S2); RecoveryClock/FillDeadline (P1.M4.T2.S1); LedPatternEngine (P1.M5.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: Pure FillEngine.step(uint32_t nowMs, ButtonEvent, averaged readings when due) -> Outputs + log-event list (state transitions, backstop computation, trip/confirm events — consumed by the integration loop's logLine). Orchestrate sub-phases; on Idle+Short: compute backstop, run settle/baseline (fault path if implausible — valve never opened), open valve + anchor deadline, led Solid; on trip: valve close -> Confirm; on second trip within window: Done, record recovery reference at valve-close instant, led DonePulse; on abort: close valve, record fill end, Idle. Native tests: full happy path with scripted sensor streams (sensor1 first, then sensor2 first — symmetric); Flow 1 (start -> abort -> restart with fresh RECOMPUTED timer, section 5.2); Flow 2 complete; confirm-window timeout -> fault; ordering assertion: every Filling/Confirm exit emits valve close as the first output action.
4. OUTPUT: single FillEngine consumed by the hardware integration loop (P1.M6.T2.S1).
5. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: Fault latching and blink codes 1/2/3 (pure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 7 fault table: code 1 = sensor 1 bad (baseline out of range, false trip, never tripped in confirm window); code 2 = sensor 2 bad (same); code 3 = timer fired with no trip. Cadence handled by LedPatternEngine.FaultBlink(n). Faults LATCH: cleared only by RESET or power cycle — which also clears tank history so the next fill uses the 30-min default (section 5.3); BOOT is ignored while faulted; the valve refuses to open while faulted (structurally guaranteed — Fault never transitions to Filling).
2. INPUT: FillEngine from P1.M6.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Extend FillEngine: fault entry closes the valve FIRST, sets state Fault with code, led FaultBlink(code). Native tests: baseline out-of-range on sensor 1 -> code 1 and valve NEVER opened; sensor 2 confirm-window miss -> code 2; backstop expiry with no trip -> code 3; early-trip/early-wet guards (P1.M3.T3.S2) map to the sensor's code; button events in Fault change nothing and never open the valve; a fresh engine instance (simulating reset) starts Idle with no history -> next fill uses 30 min.
4. OUTPUT: complete latching fault behavior inside FillEngine — the behavioral contract of sections 5, 7 fully closed.
5. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: Property tests: no auto-open, valve LOW first, close-on-every-exit
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Section 10 checklist maps to testable properties: (a) valve pin driven LOW as the very first line of setup(); (b) valve opens only in Filling, entered only by human BOOT press — no boot, watchdog reset, fault-recovery or button path auto-opens; (c) hang -> watchdog reset -> valve closed -> Idle awaiting press; (d) no delay() in the fill loop; (e) backstops hug real fill times (covered by P1.M4.T1.S1 table tests).
2. INPUT: FillEngine + integration firmware from P1.M6.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Native tests: seeded randomized event+sensor sequences (thousands of steps) asserting valveOpen never becomes true except via Idle+ShortPress; every transition out of Filling/Confirm emits valve-close as first output; initial output = valve LOW, state Idle. Structural check: a tiny script (test/check_setup_first_line.py or a grep assertion) verifying setup()'s first executable statement drives PIN_VALVE LOW, and that delay( does not appear outside comments in the ARDUINO loop region. Watchdog-reset behavior verified on bench in P1.M7.T2.S1 (a fresh boot lands Idle/valve-closed — natively: fresh engine instance starts Idle with valve LOW).
4. OUTPUT: green invariant suite guarding all future refactors; CI-runnable via pio test -e native plus the structural check.
5. DOCS: none — tests only.
